name: manual_763088
claim: commit_clean_test.sh (scripts/git/commit-clean.sh ~line 108-111) fails with 'verify_args[@]: unbound variable' on macOS's stock /bin/bash (3.2, frozen for GPLv2 licensing) when neither --allow-empty nor --amend is set, leaving verify_args as an empty array. Empty-array expansion under 'set -u' throws unbound-variable on bash <4.4 but is safe on bash >=4.4 (a documented bash behavior change) -- so this test passes in CI/newer-bash environments and fails locally on unmodified macOS. Pre-existing on origin/main, not introduced by any session change. Fix: use the unset-safe expansion "\" (or check array length before expanding, or require bash>=4.4 explicitly) in commit-clean.sh.

decisions.notes: Found 2026-07-30 while verifying scripts/git/commit_clean_test.sh after PT PR #300 fixes -- test failed locally with this exact unbound-variable error even though Cursor's own automated review of the same PR reported 'all passed' for the identical test file, confirming this is a bash-version-dependent flake (stock macOS bash 3.2 vs whatever newer bash Cursor's review environment used), not a regression from PR #300's changes. Not yet fixed -- filed as a known issue for whoever picks it up next.
